english: Master, the wheel broke. How shall we carry the grain home? I make a new wheel from birch wood. I need an awl and a knife. The awl is in the house. Your son took the knife. Where did he go? He is catching fish at the river with a net/bundle. Now I wait for him, and you cook the fish.

Kind-minded one, at night I saw in dreams. What did you see? A white horse stood at the door and spoke to me. What did it say? It said this: the year will be good. The gods give us a good year. Now stand up. The stable waits.

Granddaughter, sit with me by the fire. Tell me: what do you see? An eagle over the lake, and it seized a fish. What did grandfather see? I saw nothing; I slept under the oak. The old men sit, and the young women and wives work. You smile. Sing me a song and I will sleep.

Grandmother, teach me. How do you weave? I stretch the threads. Now I weave the wool through them. That I do. Give the wool to the guest. You lead the thread. Is the plaited basket empty for me? It is empty. Soon you will grow/fill it. To whom will you give it? I give it to my sister.
uncertain: téntum mē déwks: prohibitive 'don't pull the thread'?

english: Grandmother told me a tale. Tell it to me. What did you do this day? I guarded the lambs and caught a hare. Did you catch the hare for the guests? Yes, I caught it for the guests. The dog drove it to me. Now hear the tale of the hare and the wolf. The wolf chases the hare. Did he catch it? The hare is swifter than the wolf. He did not.

Old man, I drove (them) from the field to the stable. How many sheep did you drive? I drove ten sheep and three lambs. Four lambs are from early spring. Where did the few/shepherd go? I don't know. An eagle flew over the enclosure. A weak(?) lamb does not live through the night. Go and look for it. I go. The dog will come with me.
